# Lithon

> Lithon is a Python library and native x86-64 execution engine. Every supported program carries fixed-width type annotations, is statically verified before it runs, and executes as generated machine code with no LLVM and no runtime package.

Lithon is a Python library and native x86-64 execution engine. Source files use the `.lio` extension. Every program is statically verified before it runs; a program the backend cannot prove is refused rather than guessed at.

## The one rule

> If Lithon cannot prove that a program satisfies the rules required by its native backend, it refuses native compilation rather than guessing.

## Type system in one block

```
int[8]  int[16]  int[32]  int[64]   signed, fixed width
float[64]                        IEEE-754 binary64 (float[32] is refused)
bool                              1 byte, reads back as 0/1
str[N]                            N bytes, NUL-terminated, bounded
list[T, N]                        fixed capacity N
tuple[T, N]                       fixed length N, homogeneous
dict[K, V, B]                     B buckets, B must be a power of two
ptr[T]                            typed pointer, variable name needs a leading _
class P(Struct)                   packed fields, no padding
class E(Enum)                    a tag plus the largest payload
```

There is no bare `int`, no `uint`, no `None`, no `lambda`, no closure, no `set`, no `bytes`, no `Optional`/`Union`, no `**`, no `//`, no `<=`/`>=`, and no chained comparison.

## A small program

```python
x: int[64] = 10
y: int[64] = 20

result: int[64] = x + y

print(result)
```

## Documentation index

### Start here

From zero to a natively running program.

- [Welcome to Lithon](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/welcome)[essential] — Understand what Lithon is, what it refuses to do, and why the refusal is the feature.
- [Hello, native](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/hello-world)[essential] — Write, verify and run your first natively-executed program end to end.
- [Build & install](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/installation) — Build the engine and prove the install works.
- [The mental model](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/mental-model)[essential] — Hold the one rule that makes the rest of the language checkable: prove before you run.

### The language

Types, flow, functions, containers, unsafe memory.

- [Types & widths](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/types)[essential] — Pick the right width for every value, and know which conversions are legal.
- [Declarations & assignment](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/declarations)[essential] — Give every name a type and a value, and be refused when you have not.
- [Control flow](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/control-flow)[essential] — Write every branch and loop the language supports, and know which ones it does not.
- [Functions](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/functions)[essential] — Give a function a contract the compiler can check, and call it safely.
- [Operators](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/operators)[essential] — Predict the result of every expression, including the ones that surprise CPython.
- [Containers](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/containers)[essential] — Model fixed-size data without a heap, and know each container's rules.
- [Pointers](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/pointers) — Reach raw memory deliberately, with the naming rule that keeps it visible.
- [Structs](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/structs)[essential] — Lay out packed storage whose bytes match a C struct exactly.
- [Enums](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/enums)[essential] — Model a tagged union and read it back safely with match.
- [Methods](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/methods) — Give a struct behaviour, and understand why it is inlined.
- [Type Functions](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/type-functions)[reference] — Build reusable types at compile time.
- [Syscalls](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/syscalls)[reference] — Call the kernel directly, with the argument rules both tiers agree on.
- [Divergences from Python](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/python-divergences)[essential] — Port Python code without being surprised by a silent semantic change.
- [Exceptions & traps](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/exceptions)[essential] — Recover from the seven engine traps and know the rest is refused.
- [match](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/match)[essential] — Dispatch on an enum exhaustively, and read a variant's payload safely.
- [Strings](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/strings)[essential] — Use bounded byte runs without a heap or an allocator.
- [Networking](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/networking)[reference] — Open a real socket from Lithon and pass the byte-order test.

### Inside the engine

Dual tiers, verification, SSA, optimization, SIMD.

- [Engine architecture](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/architecture)[essential] — Trace a program from .lio source to executable memory.
- [Dual-tier execution](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/dual-tier) — Understand what Tier-0 and Tier-1 each do, and when each runs.
- [The type checker](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/typechecking) — Read a diagnostic and know exactly which rule you broke.
- [Optimizer & SSA pipeline](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/pipeline)[reference] — See the optimizer and SSA passes that run before the encoder.
- [SIMD auto-vectorization](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/simd)[reference] — Know when a loop becomes AVX2 and why the result is still exact.

### Reference

Errors, builtins, verification gate, honest limits.

- [Errors & diagnostics](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/errors)[essential] — Look up any error code and what it means.
- [Built-in functions](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/builtins)[essential] — Look up any built-in, its signature and its rules.
- [Semantics](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/semantics)[essential] — Look up the exact meaning of the operations that surprise people.
- [Verification](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/verification) — Check the claims instead of taking them on trust.
- [Honest limits](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/limits)[essential] — Know exactly what is not implemented yet.

### Machine view

For enthusiasts: IR, registers, x86-64 encodings.

- [Source to machine](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/source-to-machine) — Read the IR and the machine code for any example.
- [Registers & ABI](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/registers-abi)[reference] — Know where every argument and return value lives.
- [Instruction encoding](https://project-lithon.github.io/Lithon/docs/instruction-encoding)[reference] — Read the encoder's output byte by byte.
